questions.q: Where were Ginger and the other chestnut horse sent after they were sold to a fashionable gentleman?
choices: London
Brighton
Birtwick Park
A farm by the railway

questions.q: Ginger says a check-rein held her head up "for hours together." What was a check-rein?
choices: A rein that forced a horse to hold its head up high
A rope used to tie a horse to a post in the yard
A soft halter used for leading a young foal
A long rein that jockeys use only when racing
questions.evidence: if you tossed your head up high and were obliged to hold it there

questions.q: Why did the coachman and his master rein Ginger so tightly?
choices: They thought it made the horses look more stylish
They believed it helped the horses trot much faster
It kept the horses' heads warm in the cold wind
A horse doctor told them it was good for the neck
questions.evidence: thinking we looked more stylish so

questions.q: What happened when Ginger fretted or stamped while waiting at a grand party?
choices: The whip was laid on
She was given a bran mash
She was taken home early
The lady came out to pat her

questions.q: How did Ginger's time with the London gentleman end?
choices: She plunged and kicked and broke a lot of harness
She ran away in the park and upset the carriage
She fell sick and was sent off to the country
The coachman liked her and bought her for himself
questions.evidence: I soon broke a lot of harness, and kicked myself clear

questions.q: How did the second dealer find out how to manage Ginger?
choices: He tried other bits and drove her with no check-rein
He whipped her hard every day until she behaved
He wrote to Samson Ryder to ask for his advice
He turned her out in a field for a whole year
questions.evidence: At last he drove me quite without a check-rein

questions.q: Why did Ginger bite the new groom at the country gentleman's place?
choices: He was rough and hit her with a broom or fork
He kept forgetting to give her any oats or hay
He rode her much too fast on the hard roads
He took away her rug on the coldest nights
questions.evidence: he would hit me above the hocks with his stable broom or the fork

questions.q: What did Ginger believe about men by the time she came to Birtwick?
choices: That men were her natural enemies
That nearly all men were kind to horses
That only young boys were ever cruel
That men could never ride a horse well

questions.q: What did James do after Ginger bit him, following John's advice?
choices: Brought her a bran mash and stroked her
Gave her a sharp cut with the whip
Asked the master to sell her at once
Stopped going into her stall at all
questions.evidence: brought me a bran mash and stroked me

questions.q: What were John's joking "Birtwick horseballs" really made of?
choices: Patience, gentleness, firmness, petting and sense
Oats, bran, treacle, honey and a little linseed oil
Powders and pills that the horse doctor sent over
Chopped apples, carrots and sugar rolled together
questions.evidence: made up of patience and gentleness, firmness and petting
